newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd shareholders approve P&O deal.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd shareholders approve P&O deal.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV said on Friday its shareholders had approved the $1.5 billion container shipping merger with Peninsula and Oriental Steam Navigation Co .
The company also welcomed today's decision of the European Commission (EU) to approve the merger.
"The new company, P&O Nedlloyd, can therefore now proceed as planned from 1 January, 1997," Nedlloyd said.
"This is very good news. It will enable the company to maintain the momentum built up over the last few weeks, so that it will be fully operational at the start of 1997."

P&O and Nedlloyd announced on September 9 that they would merge their container businesses to form a joint venture company with an annual turnover of almost $4.0 billion and a net asset value of $1.5 billion.
The new company will be one of the largest container shipping operators in the world, with more direct ports of call and a wider range of trade routes than any other operator.
The EU cleared the merger after finding that the new group would not dominate its markets.
